log_text: First wax harvest from the langstroth hive. Crude cappings and broken comb. Melted in a water bath — the wax floated, the propolis and debris sank. Poured through a cotton cloth while still liquid. Cooled to a disc: amber-clear, slight honey smell. Better than expected.

Second clarification pass on the same wax lot — re-melted and floated twice through clean water. The second float removed residual cloudiness. Result is pale amber, nearly transparent in thin section. The smell is cleaner. Stored in a sealed clay cup.

Second hive harvest — more propolis contamination than the first. The wax came out dark amber even after one float. Smells strongly of propolis and old honey. Functional but not clean-burning. Blended with rabbit tallow to lower the melting point and extend the volume.

Three passes on the dark lot from the second harvest. Each pass lighter than the last. After the third float: amber-clear, acceptable burn quality. The triple process used more heat but the wax improved significantly. Worth doing for candle stock.

Old cappings stored for two months before processing. The wax had crystallised partially in the cold storage. Re-melting took longer. Float clarification went cleanly — the stored wax had less propolis than fresh. Pale amber result. Six candle discs stored flat.

Scrap wax — pieces scraped from the hive frames and floor boards. Too much debris for the float method alone. Pressed through cloth while molten. Still dark and cloudy. Not suitable for clean-burning candles but adequate for waterproofing cloth and sealing leather joints.

Blended clarified wax with twenty percent rabbit tallow. The blend melts at a lower temperature — better for the shelter climate which runs cold. Burns slightly smokier than pure wax but the soft candles do not need re-dipping as often. A practical compromise.

Tested burning a pure clarified beeswax candle against a tallow-blend candle. The pure wax burned longer, cleaner, and brighter. The tallow blend produced more soot but lasted a similar time. Both are useful. Pure wax for when clarity matters; blend for when quantity matters.
